main_conclusions: Existing historical data are sufficient to support that fixed readk4 is not a global default.
cb256-r8 has the strongest fixed-readk4 local positive evidence: readk2 spread 0.184 versus readk4 all-completed spread 0.010.
cb256-r4 also supports fixed-readk4 as a local positive: ordinary readk2 r1 spread 0.18391015625 versus formal readk4 all-completed spread 0.015.
cb64-r16 is a high-path damage counterexample: readk4 s124 r1/r2 are 0.831 and 0.849, versus readk2 s124 replacement 0.959.
cb128-r8 is a reproducibility counterexample: readk4 main pair is 0.973/0.972, but s125 rerun is 0.609.
Immediate broad rerun is not needed for the qualitative boundary claim; targeted runs are only needed if promoting cb256-r4/r8 readk4 to formal three-seed candidates.
known_gaps: Fixed-readk4 seed123 is missing for cb256-r8 and cb256-r4 formalization.
cb128-r8 fixed-readk4 seed123 is missing for a complete three-seed failure map.
Historical rows lack read margin, read entropy, candidate churn, and per-head read telemetry.
Future runs should explicitly write both best and final metrics to artifacts.
